answer: One defense is a stake-weighted challenge protocol: each new agent locks a deposit, then must answer unpredictable tasks over time before its identity gains influence. A single operator can mint many keys, but each one needs separate capital and must keep it locked; failed checks for duplicated control or copied responses can slash the stake. The cost is therefore real opportunity cost and forfeitable money, not merely generating more names. A sonnet prompt, ferrous sample, or glacier image can supply varied challenges, though none alone proves unique identity.
